correctness.rationale: Stationarity against arbitrary antiderivatives of \(V\) gives \(\mathbb E[g_K(V-V_K)W\mid V]=F(V)\). Stationarity against arbitrary antiderivatives of \(W\), after weighting by the positive rate \(q(V)\), gives \(\mathbb E_\nu[W_\infty(V)\mid W]=W\). In each case the coordinate derivative is exactly the regression residual up to its displayed positive scale, so conditional orthogonality gives the two variance defects. Zero voltage defect makes \(V\) constant and bounded completeness of the scalar gate relaxation forces equilibrium. Zero gate defect makes \(W\) constant; strict monotonicity of \(W_\infty\) then makes \(V\) constant. The packaged checker verifies the residual-variance and measure-tilt algebra exactly.

value.rationale: Morris–Lecar is a canonical planar conductance model whose phase-plane interpretation is organized by the voltage and recovery nullclines. The accepted theorem gives those geometric curves an exact stationary-statistical meaning: potassium current is calibrated on every voltage fiber, while the recovery nullcline is calibrated after the intrinsic gate-rate tilt. The variance gaps quantify exactly how much stationary fluctuation remains beyond each nullcline predictor and identify that gap with mean-square coordinate speed. This yields direct consistency checks for periodic-orbit or stationary simulation data and a complete equilibrium equality class, without merely recomputing a bifurcation threshold or known phase portrait.
